messages:
maria.g: Heads up — we've been seeing batch-size oscillation after node reclaims/scaleups that correlates with 99.9% tail latency spikes (~300ms). Observed on canary region and a couple of prod shards.
kevin: Can you paste a short trace or logs? Sounds like slow-start ripple.
maria.g: Here’s a small log slice around a scale event. note how batch sizes jump -> drop -> overshoot.
```
2026-03-18T10:12:01Z INFO node manager: pool scaled +2
2026-03-18T10:12:04Z DEBUG batcher: accepted 128 tokens into batch (tenant=search-1)
2026-03-18T10:12:04Z DEBUG batcher: flush triggered size=128 deadline=25ms
2026-03-18T10:12:04Z INFO executor: start dispatch (batch=128)
2026-03-18T10:12:04Z DEBUG batcher: enqueue after dispatch size=5
2026-03-18T10:12:04Z DEBUG batcher: coalesce window extended -> 50ms
2026-03-18T10:12:05Z DEBUG batcher: accepted 90 tokens into batch (tenant=search-1)
2026-03-18T10:12:05Z DEBUG batcher: flush triggered size=90 deadline=25ms
```
kevin: Hmm — that pattern smells like "slow-start then greedy enqueue" from clients + the batcher not having anti-starvation shaping.
samir: Agreed. We also saw something similar with the tiny-window fastpath where small requests starve when large rampups happen.
anya: Can we differentiate two issues: (1) oscillation due to global headroom reallocation, and (2) short-term starvation of small requests after a big flush? They require different fixes.
maria.g: Good split. My hypothesis: when capacity returns (new GPU/slot), the admission layer lets large queued requests in aggressively to fill throughput; batcher coalesces aggressively, then when those large batches finish, backlog drops and the next arrivals are small, but we still have coalescing-tuned for large batches so small ones wait -> increased latency. Repeat.
kevin: Proposed mitigations: (A) slow-start for newly allocated capacity that ramps allowed batch size exponentially over X seconds, (B) anti-starvation throttle that reserves N micro-slots per tenant to serve small requests immediately, (C) hysteresis on coalesce window and batch-size target to avoid flip-flopping.
samir: Implementation complexity: A is global admission plus per-executor ramp state; B needs per-tenant or per-route accounting; C is simpler (just smoothing). Tradeoffs: A reduces throughput ramp but stabilizes latency; B reduces maximum throughput slightly because of reserved headroom.
anya: We should also consider a cheap heuristic first: when a flush happens with size > S, temporarily lower `coalesce_window_ms` for the next T ms so we avoid immediate huge coalesces, letting small requests through. Low-risk rollback.
kevin: I like an incremental approach: start with heuristic (anya) + add per-tenant micro-slot (B) as opt-in for high-p80-sensitive tenants. If that looks good, evaluate slow-start ramp (A) for cluster-level behavior.
maria.g: Experiment plan:
- rollout A/B to canary only: enable micro-slot = 4 tokens per tenant, coalesce-hysteresis smoothing = 0.7 alpha, heuristic window-reduce after big-flush (S=80, T=200ms).
- metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail-request-queue-length, batch-size distribution histogram, throughput (tokens/s), fairness (median latency by request-size).
- duration: 72 hours of traffic plus deliberate scale events reproduced in staging.
kevin: How do we expose flags? Runtime config in console per deployment + per-tenant opt-in. Something like: 
```
batching: {
  anti_starvation_slots: 4,
  coalesce_alpha: 0.7,
  post_big_flush_cooldown_ms: 200
}
```
samir: Add a telemetry tag `batch_ramp_state` to traces so we can correlate slow-start ramp phases with tail latencies.
anya: Also add a synthetic test in the perf harness that simulates scale-up with mixed small+large requests to validate no oscillation.
build-bot: deploy canary config created: rollout/batching-oscillation-mitigation canary -> started at 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z
maria.g: Assignments: I’ll own the canary run and dashboards. @kevin will prototype the micro-slot accounting. @samir add telemetry/trace tags. @anya add perf harness scenario. Follow-up sync Friday 11am PT.
kevin: Quick note on fairness math: micro-slots should be weighted by token-size, not request-count, otherwise tiny requests would get too much headroom. Keep it token-aware.
samir: Agreed. Also ensure we cap reserved slots so we don't starve bulk-optimized tenants. Maybe a soft-share approach: min(reserved, tenant_token_quota*0.1).
anya: Sounds good. If the canary reduces p99 by >20% without reducing throughput by >5% -> propose progressive rollout.
maria.g: Thanks all — creating the RFC-lite doc and linking results here once canary completes. :thumbsup:
kevin: Thanks — will start a small PR for micro-slot prototype today.
anya: Will add the perf scenario now.
samir: I'll instrument traces and add dashboards.
maria.g: Closing the thread for now; will reopen with canary results.
